title.en: Volume 394 Biographies 181: Xu Guangjin, Ye Mingchen, Huang Zonghan
title.raw: 卷394 列傳一百八十一 徐广缙 葉名琛 黄宗汉

sentences.zh: 列傳一百八十一

translations.literal: Biographies 181
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 181

sentences.zh: 徐廣縉葉名琛黃宗漢

translations.literal: Xu Guangjin, Ye Mingchen, Huang Zonghan
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guangjin, Ye Mingchen, and Huang Zonghan

sentences.zh: 徐廣縉，字仲升，河南鹿邑人。

translations.literal: Xu Guangjin, style name Zhongsheng, was a man of Luyi in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guangjin, whose courtesy name was Zhongsheng, came from Luyi in Henan.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二十五年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，遷御史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, was appointed compiler, and was transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the twenty-fifth year of the Jiaqing reign, entered the Hanlin Academy as a probationer compiler, received appointment as a regular compiler, and was later transferred to the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 道光十三年，出為陝西榆林知府，歷安徽徽寧池太道、江西督糧道、福建按察使。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Daoguang he went out as prefect of Yulin in Shaanxi, and successively served as intendant of Huaining-Chizhou-Taiping in Anhui, grain superintendent of Jiangxi, and provincial judicial commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Daoguang he was posted as prefect of Yulin in Shaanxi, then served in turn as the Anhui circuit intendant for Huaining, Chizhou, and Taiping, as Jiangxi grain superintendent, and as Fujian provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 擢順天府尹，尋出為四川布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to governor of Shuntian Prefecture, and soon after went out as provincial administrative commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to governor of Shuntian Prefecture and shortly thereafter appointed provincial administrative commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，服闋，補江寧布政使。

translations.literal: He mourned his mother; when the mourning period ended he was reassigned as provincial administrative commissioner of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he observed mourning, and when the mourning period ended he was reassigned as Jiangning administrative commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，擢雲南巡撫，調廣東。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was promoted to governor of Yunnan and transferred to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of the reign he was promoted to governor of Yunnan and then transferred to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，擢兩廣總督，兼通商大臣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was promoted to governor-general of Liangguang, concurrently serving as superintendent of trade.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was elevated to governor-general of the Two Guang and concurrently appointed superintendent of foreign trade.

sentences.zh: 自江寧定約五口通商，許廣州省城設立棧房，領事入城，以平禮相待。

translations.literal: Since the Nanjing treaty had opened five ports to trade, Guangzhou provincial city was permitted to establish warehouses, and consuls were to enter the city and be received with equal courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Nanjing treaty, which opened five ports to trade, the provincial city of Guangzhou was allowed to set up merchant warehouses, and foreign consuls were to enter the city and be received on a basis of equal ceremonial standing.

sentences.zh: 粵民堅執洋人不准入城舊制，聚眾以抗，官不能解。

translations.literal: Cantonese people firmly upheld the old rule that foreigners must not enter the city, gathered in crowds to resist, and officials could not resolve it.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Guangdong clung to the old prohibition against foreigners entering the city, massed in protest, and the authorities could not settle the dispute.

sentences.zh: 總督耆英既與英人議緩俟二年之後，尋內召，廣縉繼任。

translations.literal: Governor-General Keying had already agreed with the English to defer the matter for two years; soon he was recalled to the capital, and Guangjin succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Keying had already negotiated with the British to postpone entry for two years; he was soon recalled to the capital, and Guangjin took his place.

sentences.zh: 會黃竹岐鄉民毆殺英人六，領事德庇時要挾賠償保護，廣縉治殺人者罪，而拒其非理之求，戒諭人民毋暴動，事得解。

translations.literal: It happened that villagers of Huangzhuqi beat six Englishmen to death; Consul Davis demanded compensation and protection; Guangjin punished the killers but refused his unreasonable demands, admonished the people not to riot, and the affair was settled.
translations.idiomatic: When villagers at Huangzhuqi killed six British subjects, Consul Davis pressed for compensation and guarantees of protection. Guangjin punished the killers, refused his unreasonable demands, warned the populace against violence, and the crisis passed.

sentences.zh: 德庇時回國，文翰代為領事，初至請謁。

translations.literal: Davis returned to his country; Bowring replaced him as consul and on first arrival requested an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Davis went home, and Bowring succeeded him as consul; on arriving he asked for an official audience.

sentences.zh: 廣縉赴虎門閱砲台，延見之，遂登其舟，示以坦白。

translations.literal: Guangjin went to Humen to inspect the batteries, received him, then boarded his vessel to show frankness.
translations.idiomatic: Guangjin went to Humen to inspect the coastal batteries, granted him an audience, and then boarded his ship to show openness.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，文翰以兩年入城之期已屆，要踐約，廣縉諭以耆英所許。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Bowring said the two-year term for entering the city had arrived and demanded fulfillment of the agreement; Guangjin instructed him according to what Keying had promised.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year Bowring declared that the two-year deadline for entry into the city had come due and demanded that the agreement be honored; Guangjin cited the terms Keying had allowed.

sentences.zh: 乃姑為權宜之計，民情憤激，眾怒難犯，非官所能禁止。

translations.literal: He then made a temporary expedient: popular feeling was inflamed, the people's wrath was not to be provoked, and officials could not restrain it.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore offered a provisional compromise: public sentiment was explosive, mass anger could not be defied, and the government could not hold it in check.

sentences.zh: 文翰則堅持成約，且以他省入城相詰難，揚言將駕兵船至天津訴諸京師，相持不下。

translations.literal: Bowring, however, insisted on the completed agreement, and moreover used entry into cities in other provinces to press him; he declared he would sail warships to Tianjin and appeal to the capital, and the deadlock continued.
translations.idiomatic: Bowring, however, held fast to the completed treaty and challenged him by pointing to foreign entry into cities elsewhere, threatening to send warships to Tianjin to lodge a complaint in the capital; neither side would yield.

sentences.zh: 廣縉疏聞，自請嚴議。

translations.literal: Guangjin memorialized the throne and asked that he be severely punished.
translations.idiomatic: Guangjin reported the situation to the throne and asked that he himself be severely disciplined.

sentences.zh: 密詔許暫入城一次，以踐前言，不得習以為常。

translations.literal: A secret edict permitted one temporary entry into the city to fulfill the earlier promise, but it must not become customary.
translations.idiomatic: A secret edict allowed a single temporary entry to honor the earlier pledge, but forbade making it a precedent.

sentences.zh: 廣縉复疏言：「入城萬不可行。

translations.literal: Guangjin again memorialized, saying: "Entry into the city is absolutely impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Guangjin memorialized again: "Allowing entry into the city is utterly out of the question.

sentences.zh: 廣東民情剽悍，與閩、浙、江蘇不同。

translations.literal: Guangdong popular temperament is fierce, unlike Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Guangdong are far more volatile than those of Fujian, Zhejiang, or Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 阻其入城而有事，則眾志成城，尚有爪牙之可恃；

translations.literal: If entry is blocked and trouble arises, then the multitude will unite as one city, and there will still be claws and teeth to rely upon;
translations.idiomatic: If we keep them out and trouble follows, the populace will stand as one, and we will still have local forces to depend on;

sentences.zh: 許其入城而有事，則人心瓦解，必至內外之交訌。

translations.literal: if entry is permitted and trouble arises, then hearts will disintegrate, and internal and external strife will inevitably ensue.
translations.idiomatic: but if we admit them and trouble follows, morale will collapse and conflict will break out between the people and the authorities alike.

sentences.zh: 明知有害無利，詎敢輕於一試。

translations.literal: Knowing clearly there is harm without benefit, how dare one lightly try it.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the move brings harm without gain, how could I dare experiment with it?

sentences.zh: 」卒堅拒之。

translations.literal: " In the end he firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he stood firm in refusal.

sentences.zh: 英人乃集兵船三於香港，​​放小艇至海口各港測水探路，示恫喝。

translations.literal: The English then gathered three warships at Hong Kong, sent small boats to various estuary ports to sound depths and explore routes, showing intimidation.
translations.idiomatic: The British then concentrated three warships at Hong Kong and sent launches to sound the estuaries and probe the channels as a show of intimidation.

sentences.zh: 廣縉增兵守諸砲台及要隘，嚴備以待。

translations.literal: Guangjin increased troops to guard the batteries and key passes, making strict preparations to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Guangjin reinforced the batteries and strategic passes and made ready in full strength.

sentences.zh: 時民團號十萬，聲勢甚張。

translations.literal: At the time civilian militia numbered one hundred thousand in name, and their momentum was very imposing.
translations.idiomatic: Civilian militia at the time were said to number one hundred thousand, and their presence was formidable.

sentences.zh: 華商會議暫停各國貿易，密告美、法兩國領事，啟釁實由英人。

translations.literal: Chinese merchants met and resolved to suspend trade with all nations, secretly informing the American and French consuls that the provocation truly came from the English.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese merchants agreed to suspend trade with every nation and secretly told the American and French consuls that the British alone had provoked the crisis.

sentences.zh: 於是諸洋商慮受擾累，將以損失歸領事負責。

translations.literal: Thereupon the foreign merchants feared suffering disturbance, and would hold the consuls responsible for losses.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign traders then feared they would suffer for the dispute and would hold their consuls accountable for any losses.

sentences.zh: 士紳聯名致文翰，為反覆陳利害甚切。

translations.literal: Gentry and scholars jointly wrote Bowring, repeatedly stating advantages and harms with great urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Local gentry and scholars sent Bowring a joint petition, urgently setting out the stakes again and again.

sentences.zh: 文翰內受牽制，乃罷入城之議，乞照舊通商。

translations.literal: Bowring, constrained within, then abandoned the plan to enter the city and begged to trade as before.
translations.idiomatic: Bowring, pressed from within his own camp, abandoned the demand for entry and asked to resume trade on the old footing.

sentences.zh: 與要約，停市開巿皆非由官令，不進城即通商，後有反覆，仍行停止。

translations.literal: They made an agreement: stopping or opening markets was not by official order; if they did not enter the city they could trade, but if there were reversals trade would again be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: They concluded terms: halting or reopening the markets did not depend on official command; trade could continue without entry into the city, but any renewed breach would bring another shutdown.

sentences.zh: 事既定，廣縉疏聞，宣宗大悅。

translations.literal: When the matter was settled Guangjin memorialized the throne, and the Xuanzong Emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Once the affair was settled Guangjin reported to the throne, and the Daoguang Emperor was deeply gratified.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「洋務之興，將十年矣。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Foreign affairs have arisen for nearly ten years.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Foreign affairs have troubled us for nearly ten years.

sentences.zh: 沿海擾累，糜餉勞師，近雖略臻安謐，而馭之之法，剛柔未得其平，流弊因而愈出。

translations.literal: The coast has been disturbed and exhausted, funds wasted and armies wearied; recently there has been slight tranquility, yet methods of control have not balanced firmness and yielding, and abuses have therefore grown worse.
translations.idiomatic: The coastlands have been harried and drained, treasure spent and troops worn down; though matters have lately grown somewhat calmer, our handling of foreigners has not yet struck the right balance between firmness and conciliation, and new abuses keep appearing.

sentences.zh: 朕恐瀕海居民或遭蹂躪，一切隱忍待之。

translations.literal: We fear coastal inhabitants may suffer ravage, and therefore endure everything in forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: I fear the coastal population may yet be trampled underfoot, and so have borne much in patience.

sentences.zh: 昨英酋复伸入城之請，徐廣縉等悉心措理，動合機宜。

translations.literal: Yesterday the English chief again raised the request to enter the city; Xu Guangjin and others handled it with full care, every move fitting the moment.
translations.idiomatic: When the British envoy again pressed for entry into the city, Xu Guangjin and his colleagues managed the crisis with careful judgment at every step.

sentences.zh: 入城議寢，依舊通商。

translations.literal: The plan to enter the city was laid to rest, and trade continued as before.
translations.idiomatic: The entry proposal was shelved and commerce resumed on the former basis.

sentences.zh: 不折一兵，不發一矢，中外綏靖，可以久安，實深嘉悅！

translations.literal: Not a single soldier was broken, not an arrow loosed; Chinese and foreigners were pacified and long peace could be secured—truly deeply gratifying!
translations.idiomatic: Not one soldier was lost, not one arrow fired; peace was restored at home and abroad and could be made to last—truly a cause for great satisfaction!

sentences.zh: 」於是錫封廣縉一等子爵，賜雙眼花翎，是役商民一心，尤得紳士許祥光、伍崇曜之力為多，二人並被優擢。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Guangjin was enfeoffed as first-rank baron, granted the double-eyed peacock feather; in this campaign merchants and people were of one mind, especially aided by gentry Xu Xiangguang and Wu Chongyao, and both men were also specially promoted.
translations.idiomatic: " Guangjin was then ennobled as a first-class baron and awarded the double-eyed peacock feather. In this struggle merchants and commoners stood united, with particular help from the gentrymen Xu Xiangguang and Wu Chongyao; both were also given preferential promotion.

sentences.zh: 逾數月，文翰復言國王以進城未能如約，為人所輕，似覺赧顏，請為轉奏，廣縉以罷議進城之後貿易始復，豈可再申前說，拒之。

translations.literal: After several months Bowring again said the king, because entry into the city had not been fulfilled as agreed, was held in contempt and seemed ashamed, and asked that this be relayed upward; Guangjin, since trade had only resumed after abandoning entry, how could the former proposal be raised again, and refused.
translations.idiomatic: Months later Bowring wrote again that his sovereign, having failed to secure entry as promised, felt disgraced before his own people and asked that the court be informed; Guangjin replied that trade had resumed only after the entry question was dropped and refused to reopen the issue.

sentences.zh: 三十年，文翰又遺書大學士穆彰阿、耆英，遣人至上海、天津投遞。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year Bowring again sent letters to Grand Secretary Mujangga and Keying, dispatching men to deliver them at Shanghai and Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year Bowring again wrote to Grand Secretary Mujangga and Keying and sent couriers to deliver the letters at Shanghai and Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 文翰尋自赴上海，欲有所陳請，先後卻之；

translations.literal: Bowring soon went in person to Shanghai wishing to make representations, but was repeatedly turned away;
translations.idiomatic: Bowring soon went to Shanghai in person hoping to present his case, but was rebuffed each time;

sentences.zh: 乃回香港，蓋覬覦未已也。

translations.literal: then he returned to Hong Kong—for his covetous designs had not yet ceased.
translations.idiomatic: then returned to Hong Kong, his designs evidently not yet exhausted.

sentences.zh: 時兩廣盜賊蜂起，以廣西金田洪秀全為最悍。

translations.literal: At the time bandits rose everywhere in the Two Guang; Hong Xiuquan of Jintian in Guangxi was the fiercest.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry meanwhile flared across the Two Guang, and Hong Xiuquan of Jintian in Guangxi proved the most formidable.

sentences.zh: 巡撫鄭祖琛柔懦縱賊，廣縉疏劾其養筴貽患，罷之。

translations.literal: Governor Zheng Zuchen was weak and indulgent toward bandits; Guangjin memorialized impeaching him for nurturing mischief and causing harm, and had him dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zheng Zuchen was timid and indulgent toward the rebels; Guangjin impeached him for fostering trouble and had him removed.

sentences.zh: 廣東韶州、廉州匪亦蔓延，廣縉遣軍扼梧州、肇慶。

translations.literal: Bandits in Shaozhou and Qinzhou in Guangdong also spread; Guangjin sent troops to hold Wuzhou and Zhaoqing.
translations.idiomatic: Outlaws in Shaozhou and Qinzhou also spread through Guangdong, and Guangjin sent forces to block them at Wuzhou and Zhaoqing.

sentences.zh: 詔廣縉赴廣西剿辦，尋起林則徐督師，命廣縉剿捕廣東遊匪。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Guangjin to go to Guangxi to suppress them; soon Lin Zexu was recalled to command the campaign, and Guangjin was ordered to hunt roaming bandits in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Guangjin to Guangxi to suppress the rebels; Lin Zexu was soon recalled to take command, while Guangjin was told to clear roaming bandits in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，出駐高州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he went out to station at Gaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng he took the field and encamped at Gaozhou.

sentences.zh: 匪首凌十八、陳二、吳三、何茗科踞羅鏡圩及信宜，與洪秀全聲勢相倚。

translations.literal: Bandit chiefs Ling Shiba, Chen Er, Wu San, and He Mingke held Luojing Market and Xinyi, their power leaning on Hong Xiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftains Ling Shiba, Chen Er, Wu San, and He Mingke held Luojing Market and Xinyi, their strength linked to Hong Xiuquan.

sentences.zh: 廣縉遣兵進擊，殲吳三，追何茗科至貴縣擒之；

translations.literal: Guangjin sent troops to attack, destroyed Wu San, pursued He Mingke to Guixian and captured him;
translations.idiomatic: Guangjin sent troops against them, destroyed Wu San's force, and pursued He Mingke to Guixian where he was captured;

sentences.zh: 又破廉州賊顏品瑤，擒李士青。

translations.literal: he also defeated the Qinzhou bandit Yan Pinyao and captured Li Shiqing.
translations.idiomatic: he also broke the Qinzhou band led by Yan Pinyao and took Li Shiqing prisoner.

sentences.zh: 二年春，乘勝進攻羅鏡圩，擒凌十八。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year, pressing the victory he attacked Luojing Market and captured Ling Shiba.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year he pressed the advantage, stormed Luojing Market, and captured Ling Shiba.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，加太子太保。

translations.literal: When victory was reported he was given the rank of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: News of the victory brought him promotion to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 命馳赴梧州，而洪秀全大股已犯桂林，竄入湖南。

translations.literal: He was ordered to hurry to Wuzhou, but Hong Xiuquan's main force had already attacked Guilin and fled into Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to rush to Wuzhou, but Hong Xiuquan's main column had already struck Guilin and slipped into Hunan.

sentences.zh: 賽尚阿以罪黜，授廣縉欽差大臣，署理湖廣總督。

translations.literal: Sai Shang'a was dismissed for crime; Guangjin was appointed imperial commissioner and acting governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Sai Shang'a was cashiered for failure; Guangjin was named imperial commissioner and acting governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 十月，至衡州，賊攻長沙甚急，駱秉章、張亮基力守，屢挫賊，乃下竄岳州。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he reached Hengzhou; bandits pressed Changsha fiercely; Luo Bingzhang and Zhang Liangji defended stubbornly, repeatedly defeating them, and they fled down toward Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he reached Hengzhou while the rebels were battering Changsha; Luo Bingzhang and Zhang Liangji held the city, beat them back repeatedly, and drove them down toward Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 廣縉始抵長沙。

translations.literal: Guangjin had only just reached Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Guangjin had only just arrived at Changsha.

sentences.zh: 未幾。

translations.literal: Before long.
translations.idiomatic: Before long,

sentences.zh: 岳州亦陷，直犯武昌。

translations.literal: Yuezhou also fell, and they pressed straight on Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuezhou fell as well, and the rebels drove straight toward Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 廣縉進駐岳州，而漢陽、武昌相繼陷。

translations.literal: Guangjin advanced to station at Yuezhou, but Hanyang and Wuchang fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Guangjin moved up to Yuezhou, yet Hanyang and Wuchang fell one after another.

sentences.zh: 詔斥廣縉遷延不進，調度失機，株守岳州，擁兵自眾，褫職逮問，籍其家，論大辟。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked Guangjin for delay in advancing, loss of strategic opportunity, clinging to Yuezhou, amassing troops for his own ends; he was stripped of office, arrested and interrogated, his property confiscated, and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: An edict condemned Guangjin for tardy advance, missed chances, and clinging to Yuezhou while hoarding troops; he was dismissed, arrested, stripped of his household goods, and condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 三年夏，粵匪入河南境，釋廣縉，交巡撫陸應穀差遣，責令帶罪自效。

translations.literal: In the summer of the third year Guangdong bandits entered Henan; Guangjin was released and placed under Governor Lu Yinggu for assignment, ordered to redeem guilt by service.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the third year, as Guangdong rebels crossed into Henan, Guangjin was freed and placed at the disposal of Governor Lu Yinggu to earn reinstatement through service.

sentences.zh: 率兵駐歸德，防剿捻匪有功。

translations.literal: Leading troops he stationed at Guide, defending and suppressing Nian bandits with merit.
translations.idiomatic: He led troops at Guide, where his defense and campaigns against the Nian rebels won credit.

sentences.zh: 八年，命赴勝保軍營，尋予四品卿銜，留鳳陽從袁甲三剿捻匪。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was ordered to Sheng Bao's camp; soon given fourth-rank courtier rank, remaining at Fengyang with Yuan Jiasan to suppress Nian bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was sent to Sheng Bao's headquarters, soon granted fourth-rank courtier status, and remained at Fengyang with Yuan Jiasan fighting the Nian.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died not long afterward.

sentences.zh: 葉名琛，字昆臣，湖北漢陽人。

translations.literal: Ye Mingchen, style name Kunchen, was a man of Hanyang in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Mingchen, courtesy name Kunchen, was a native of Hanyang in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 道光十五年進士，選庶吉土，授編修。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the fifteenth year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 十八年，出為陝西興安知府。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he went out as prefect of Xing'an in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was posted as prefect of Xing'an in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 歷山西雁平道、江西鹽道、雲南按察使，湖南、甘肅、廣東布政使。

translations.literal: He successively served as Yanping circuit intendant in Shanxi, salt controller in Jiangxi, Yunnan provincial judicial commissioner, and provincial administrative commissioner of Hunan, Gansu, and Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Yanping circuit intendant in Shanxi, Jiangxi salt controller, Yunnan judicial commissioner, and administrative commissioner in Hunan, Gansu, and Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，擢廣東巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was promoted to governor of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was promoted to governor of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，英人欲踐入城之約，名琛偕總督徐廣縉堅執勿許，聯合民團，嚴為戒備。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year the English wished to fulfill the agreement to enter the city; Mingchen together with Governor-General Xu Guangjin firmly refused permission, united civilian militia, and made strict preparations.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, when the British sought to enforce the entry agreement, Mingchen and Governor-General Xu Guangjin stood firm in refusal, rallied the militia, and put the province on full alert.

sentences.zh: 華商自停貿易以製之，英人始寢前議。

translations.literal: Chinese merchants themselves stopped trade to restrain them, and the English then abandoned the earlier plan.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese merchants halted trade on their own to pressure the British, who then dropped the demand.

sentences.zh: 論功，封一等男爵，賜花翎。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed first-rank baron and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was ennobled as a first-class baron and given the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 三十年，平英德土匪，被優敘。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he pacified bandits in Yingde and was given preferential commendation.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he suppressed bandits in Yingde and received special commendation.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，殲羅鏡會匪吳三，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he destroyed the Luojing secret-society bandit Wu San and was made Junior Vice Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng he destroyed Wu San of the Luojing secret society and was promoted to Junior Vice Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二年，廣縉赴廣西督師，命名琛接辦羅鏡剿捕事宜，出駐高州。

translations.literal: In the second year Guangjin went to Guangxi to command troops; Mingchen was named to take over Luojing suppression, and went out to station at Gaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, when Guangjin went to Guangxi to command the campaign, Mingchen was assigned the Luojing suppression and encamped at Gaozhou.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，羅鏡匪首凌十八就殲，加總督銜，署總督，赴南、韶一帶督剿。

translations.literal: That autumn the Luojing bandit chief Ling Shiba was destroyed; he was given governor-general rank, acted as governor-general, and went to Nan and Shao to supervise suppression.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Ling Shiba of Luojing was destroyed; Mingchen received acting governor-general rank, took charge of the province, and supervised operations in the Nanxiong and Shaoguan districts.

sentences.zh: 尋實授兩廣總督，兼通商大臣。

translations.literal: Soon he was substantively appointed governor-general of Liangguang, concurrently superintendent of trade.
translations.idiomatic: He soon received full appointment as governor-general of the Two Guang and superintendent of trade.

sentences.zh: 時廣東盜賊蜂起，四年，廣州群匪擾及省城，遣將分路進剿，連戰皆捷。

translations.literal: At the time bandits swarmed in Guangdong; in the fourth year Guangzhou bandits disturbed even the provincial city; he sent generals on separate routes to attack, winning every battle.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry meanwhile engulfed Guangdong; in the fourth year gangs threatened the provincial capital itself, and he sent generals along several routes, winning a string of victories.

sentences.zh: 近省之佛山、龍門、從化、東莞、陽山、河源、增城、封川，韶州之海豐、開建，潮州之惠來，肇慶府城及德慶並陷，先後克復。

translations.literal: Nearby Foshan, Longmen, Conghua, Dongguan, Yangshan, Heyuan, Zengcheng, Fengchuan; Haifeng and Kaijian in Shaozhou; Huilai in Chaozhou; the prefectural city of Zhaoqing and Deqing—all fell and were recovered in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Districts near the capital—Foshan, Longmen, Conghua, Dongguan, Yangshan, Heyuan, Zengcheng, Fengchuan—as well as Haifeng and Kaijian in Shaozhou, Huilai in Chaozhou, and the prefectural seats of Zhaoqing and Deqing, all fell and were retaken in succession.

sentences.zh: 鄰省軍務方亟，糧餉器械多賴廣東接濟，名琛籌供無缺，益得時譽。

translations.literal: Neighboring provinces were pressed by military affairs and relied heavily on Guangdong for grain, funds, and weapons; Mingchen supplied without shortage and gained further contemporary praise.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring provinces, hard pressed by war, depended on Guangdong for grain, pay, and arms; Mingchen furnished supplies without fail and won still greater renown.

sentences.zh: 五年，以總督協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, as governor-general he was made associate grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was named associate grand secretary while retaining the governorship.

sentences.zh: 六年，拜體仁閣大學士，仍留總督任。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Birendian Pavilion, still retaining the governorship.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he entered the Grand Secretariat as a Birendian Grand Secretary but remained in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 名琛性木彊，勤吏事，屬僚憚其威重。

translations.literal: Mingchen's nature was obstinate; he was diligent in official business, and subordinates feared his authority.
translations.idiomatic: Mingchen was stubborn by nature, tireless in administration, and his subordinates stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 初以偕徐廣縉拒英人入城被殊眷，因狃於前事，頗自負，好大言，遇中外交涉事，略書數字答之，或竟不答。

translations.literal: At first, because together with Xu Guangjin he had refused English entry into the city, he received special favor; relying on that past affair he became quite self-confident, fond of grand talk; in Sino-foreign matters he would answer with a few written words, or not answer at all.
translations.idiomatic: His early success in blocking British entry with Xu Guangjin had won him the court's special trust; he grew complacent, spoke boldly, and on foreign affairs would scribble a few lines in reply—or ignore the letter altogether.

sentences.zh: 會匪之逼廣州，或議借外國兵禦賊者，斥之退。

translations.literal: When bandits pressed Guangzhou, some proposed borrowing foreign troops to repel bandits; he rebuked them and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels threatened Guangzhou, some suggested hiring foreign troops; he denounced the idea and dismissed them.

sentences.zh: 匪既平，按察使沈棣輝功最多，列上官紳兵練出力者請獎，格不奏，兵練皆解體。

translations.literal: After bandits were pacified, provincial judicial commissioner Shen Dihui had the greatest merit; he listed officials, gentry, and militia who had exerted themselves and requested rewards, but the memorial was blocked and not submitted, and the militia all disbanded.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were subdued, Judicial Commissioner Shen Dihui had done the most; Mingchen listed officials, gentry, and militia for reward but refused to forward the memorial, and the militia melted away.

sentences.zh: 又嚴治通匪餘黨，或藉捕匪仇殺，從賊逃不敢歸，其黠者投香港，勸英人攻廣州。

translations.literal: He also strictly punished remnants who had communicated with bandits; some used bandit-catching to settle private scores; those who had followed the rebels dared not return; the clever ones fled to Hong Kong and urged the English to attack Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also cracked down on collaborators; some used anti-bandit campaigns to settle scores; former followers of the rebels dared not come home, and the shrewdest fled to Hong Kong to urge the British to strike Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 會水師千總巡河，遇划艇張英國旗，搜獲十三人，拔其旗。

translations.literal: It happened that a naval lieutenant patrolling the river met a rowboat flying the British flag, searched it and seized thirteen men, and pulled down the flag.
translations.idiomatic: A naval lieutenant on river patrol then came upon a skiff flying the British flag, searched it, seized thirteen men, and tore down the flag.

sentences.zh: 英領事巴夏禮索之不得，貽書名​​琛責問，謂捕匪當移取，不當擅執，毀旗尤非禮。

translations.literal: British Consul Parkes demanded them without success, wrote Mingchen reproaching him, saying that when catching bandits one should request transfer, not seize on one's own authority, and destroying the flag was especially discourteous.
translations.idiomatic: Consul Parkes demanded their release in vain and wrote Mingchen a rebuke: bandit suspects should be handed over through proper channels, not seized at will, and tearing down the flag was an especial insult.

sentences.zh: 名琛令送十三人於領事，不受，必欲並索千總，遂置之。

translations.literal: Mingchen ordered the thirteen men sent to the consul; they were not accepted; he insisted on also demanding the lieutenant, and the matter was left unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Mingchen sent the thirteen men to the consulate, but Parkes refused them and insisted on the lieutenant as well; the affair stalled.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遣通事來告：「越日日中不如約，即攻城。

translations.literal: Before long he sent an interpreter to announce: "If the agreement is not met by noon tomorrow, the city will be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an interpreter brought word: "Unless terms are met by noon tomorrow, we will attack the city.

sentences.zh: 」至期，英兵果奪獵德、中流砲台。

translations.literal: " When the day came, English troops indeed seized the Liede and Zhongliu batteries.
translations.idiomatic: " At the appointed hour British forces seized the Liede and Zhongliu batteries.

sentences.zh: 名琛曰：「彼當自走。

translations.literal: Mingchen said: "They will leave on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Mingchen said, "They will withdraw of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 」令水師勿與戰，於是鳳皇山、海珠諸砲台皆被踞，發砲擊省城，十月朔，毀城，既入復出。

translations.literal: " He ordered the navy not to fight; thereupon Fenghuang Hill, Haizhu, and other batteries were all occupied; they fired on the provincial city; on the first day of the tenth month they breached the wall, entered, and withdrew again.
translations.idiomatic: " He forbade the navy to engage; the British then took Fenghuang Hill, Haizhu, and the other forts, shelled the city, and on the first day of the tenth month breached the wall, entered, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 遣廣州知府往詰用兵之故，英人曰：「兩國官不晤，情不親。

translations.literal: He sent the prefect of Guangzhou to reproach them for using troops; the English said: "Officials of the two countries do not meet, so feelings are not close.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the Guangzhou prefect to demand why force had been used; the British replied, "Our officials never meet, so there is no mutual trust.

sentences.zh: 誤聽傳言，屢乖和好。

translations.literal: Misled by rumors, good relations have repeatedly been broken.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors have misled us and good relations have been broken again and again.

sentences.zh: 請入城面議。

translations.literal: They asked to enter the city for face-to-face discussion.
translations.idiomatic: They asked to enter the city for a face-to-face meeting.

sentences.zh: 」名琛勿許。

translations.literal: " Mingchen would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: " Mingchen refused.

sentences.zh: 請於城外會議，亦不許。

translations.literal: They asked to confer outside the city, and that too was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed talks outside the walls, and he refused that as well.

sentences.zh: 兵練數万來援，怵敵火器，不能力戰。

translations.literal: Militia numbering tens of thousands came to aid, but fearing the enemy's firearms they could not fight vigorously.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of militia arrived to help, but they shrank from the enemy's firearms and could not fight effectively.

sentences.zh: 民憤甚，焚英、法、美三國居室，凡昔十三行皆燼。

translations.literal: Popular anger was extreme; they burned the residences of the English, French, and Americans; all the former Thirteen Factories were reduced to ashes.
translations.idiomatic: Public fury ran high; mobs burned the quarters of the British, French, and Americans, and the old Thirteen Factories district was left in ruins.

sentences.zh: 英兵亦焚民居數千家，退泊大黃，各報其國。

translations.literal: English troops also burned several thousand civilian houses, withdrew to anchor at Dahuang, and each reported to their country.
translations.idiomatic: British troops burned thousands of homes in return, withdrew to Dahuang anchorage, and each power reported home.

sentences.zh: 英遣額羅金來粵，聚兵澳門、香港，貽書索償款。

translations.literal: England sent Elgin to Guangdong, gathered troops at Macau and Hong Kong, and sent letters demanding indemnity.
translations.idiomatic: Britain sent Lord Elgin to Guangdong, concentrated forces at Macau and Hong Kong, and demanded compensation in writing.

sentences.zh: 名琛以其言狂悖，不答。

translations.literal: Mingchen, because his words were arrogant and rebellious, did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Mingchen judged the demands insolent and ignored them.

sentences.zh: 法、美兩國領事亦索賠償，且告英兵已決計攻城，原居間排解。

translations.literal: The French and American consuls also demanded compensation, and moreover informed that English troops had already decided to attack the city and originally wished to mediate.
translations.idiomatic: The French and American consuls pressed for compensation as well, warning that British forces had resolved on an assault and offering to mediate.

sentences.zh: 名琛慮其合以脅我，亦不聽；

translations.literal: Mingchen feared they would combine to coerce China and would not listen;
translations.idiomatic: Mingchen feared a joint ultimatum and would not heed them;

sentences.zh: 且不設備。

translations.literal: nor did he make preparations.
translations.idiomatic: nor did he make any defensive preparations.

sentences.zh: 七年，英兵攻東莞，總兵董開慶與戰，軍潰。

translations.literal: In the seventh year English troops attacked Dongguan; Brigadier Dong Kaiqing fought them and the army was routed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year British forces struck Dongguan; Brigadier Dong Kaiqing met them in battle and his troops were routed.

sentences.zh: 額羅金遣艇遞照會，名琛答以通商而外，概不能從。

translations.literal: Elgin sent a boat to deliver a formal note; Mingchen replied that apart from trade nothing else could be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Elgin sent a launch with an official note; Mingchen answered that trade alone could be discussed—nothing else.

sentences.zh: 累疏言：「英國主厭兵，粵事皆額羅金等所為。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized, saying: "The British sovereign dislikes war; Guangdong affairs are all the doing of Elgin and others.
translations.idiomatic: In repeated memorials he insisted: "The British queen abhors war; the Guangdong crisis is entirely the work of Elgin and his circle.

sentences.zh: 臣始終堅持，彼窮當自伏。

translations.literal: Your servant has held firm throughout; when they are cornered they will submit of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: I have stood firm throughout; once they are cornered they will yield on their own.

sentences.zh: 」密詔戒勿輕視，猶信其事有把握，仍褒勉之。

translations.literal: " A secret edict warned him not to take the enemy lightly, yet still believed the affair was under control and continued to praise and encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: " A secret edict warned him not to underestimate the enemy, yet the throne still believed he had matters in hand and continued to commend him.

sentences.zh: 九月，英兵驟至，法、美兵皆從。

translations.literal: In the ninth month English troops arrived suddenly, and French and American troops followed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month British forces appeared without warning, with French and American troops in their train.

sentences.zh: 將軍司道商戰守，名琛惟恃通事張云同為內應，待敵窮蹙。

translations.literal: The general, provincial officials, and merchants discussed war and defense; Mingchen relied only on the interpreter Zhang Yuntong as an inside contact, waiting for the enemy to be cornered.
translations.idiomatic: The general, provincial officials, and merchants debated strategy; Mingchen trusted only his interpreter Zhang Yuntong for intelligence and waited for the enemy to collapse.

sentences.zh: 民間見其夷然不驚，事皆秘不宣示，轉疑其陽拒陰撫，人心益渙。

translations.literal: Among the people, seeing him utterly unmoved, affairs all kept secret and not announced, they came instead to suspect he outwardly refused but inwardly appeased, and popular hearts grew more scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The public, seeing him unruffled while he kept everything secret, suspected he was refusing in public while appeasing in private, and morale frayed further.

sentences.zh: 十一月，敵張榜城外，限二十四時破城，勸商民遷避。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the enemy posted proclamations outside the city, giving twenty-four hours to breach the walls, urging merchants and people to move away.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the allies posted notices outside the walls, threatening to take the city within twenty-four hours and urging merchants and residents to flee.

sentences.zh: 砲擊總督署，延燒市廛，城遂陷。

translations.literal: They shelled the governor-general's yamen, the fire spread through the markets, and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Shells struck the governor-general's compound, flames swept the markets, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 巡撫柏貴檄紳士伍崇曜等議和，名琛猶持不許入城之議，夜避左都統署，英人大索得之，舁登舟。

translations.literal: Governor Bai Gui ordered gentry Wu Chongyao and others to discuss peace; Mingchen still held to the policy of not permitting entry into the city, fled by night to the Left Metropolitan Banner commander's office; the English searched widely and found him, carried him aboard ship.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Bai Gui summoned Wu Chongyao and other gentry to negotiate; Mingchen still clung to the no-entry policy and hid overnight at the Left Metropolitan Banner commander's yamen. The British hunted him down and carried him aboard ship.

sentences.zh: 將軍、巡撫以聞，詔斥名琛剛愎自用，辦理乖謬，褫其職，英人遂踞省城，禁巡撫等官不得出，責以安民。

translations.literal: The general and governor reported; an edict rebuked Mingchen for stubborn self-will and mishandling, stripped his office; the English then occupied the provincial city, forbade the governor and other officials to leave, and charged them to pacify the people.
translations.idiomatic: The general and governor reported upward; an edict condemned Mingchen's obstinacy and blunders and removed him from office. The British seized the provincial city, confined Bai Gui and other officials inside, and ordered them to keep the peace.

sentences.zh: 民各集團練，設總局於佛山，相持數年。

translations.literal: The people each gathered militia, established a headquarters at Foshan, and faced off for several years.
translations.idiomatic: Locals formed militia companies and set up a headquarters at Foshan, holding the line for years.

sentences.zh: 各國聯師赴天津，事乃益棘矣。

translations.literal: The allied armies of various nations went to Tianjin, and the affair grew still more critical.
translations.idiomatic: Allied fleets then moved on Tianjin, and the crisis deepened still further.

sentences.zh: 名琛既被虜，英人挾至印度孟加拉，居之鎮海樓上。

translations.literal: After Mingchen was captured, the English took him to Bengal in India and lodged him in the Zhenhai Tower.
translations.idiomatic: Once captured, the British took Mingchen to Bengal in India and confined him in the Zhenhai Tower.

sentences.zh: 猶時作書畫，自署曰「海上蘇武」，賦詩見志，日誦呂祖經不輟。

translations.literal: He still sometimes made calligraphy and painting, signing himself "Su Wu of the Sea," composing poetry to express his will, daily reciting the Scripture of Patriarch Lü without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He still painted and wrote, signing himself "Su Wu upon the Sea," composed verses to declare his resolve, and chanted the Scripture of Patriarch Lü daily without fail.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒，乃歸其屍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died, and then his corpse was returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he died, and his body was sent home.

sentences.zh: 粵人憾其誤國，為之語曰：「不戰、不和、不守，不死、不降、不走；

translations.literal: Cantonese resented his harm to the state and made a saying of him: "No fighting, no peace, no defense; no death, no surrender, no flight;
translations.idiomatic: Cantonese, bitter over the ruin he brought, coined a jingle: "He would not fight, negotiate, or defend; he would not die, surrender, or flee;

sentences.zh: 相臣度量，疆臣抱負；

translations.literal: a minister's measure, a frontier official's ambition;
translations.idiomatic: a grand minister's forbearance, a frontier governor's resolve;

sentences.zh: 古之所無，今之罕有。

translations.literal: what antiquity never had, what today is rarely seen.
translations.idiomatic: unknown in antiquity, scarcely matched today.

sentences.zh: 黃宗漢，字壽臣，福建晉江人。

translations.literal: Huang Zonghan, style name Shouchen, was a man of Jinjiang in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zonghan, courtesy name Shouchen, came from Jinjiang in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 道光十五年進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination and was selected as Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi in the fifteenth year of Daoguang and entered the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 散館改兵部主事，充軍機章京。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the academy he was changed to a principal clerk in the Ministry of War and served as a secretarial clerk in the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving the academy he was posted as a principal clerk in the Ministry of War and served on the Grand Council secretariat.

sentences.zh: 歷員外郎、郎中，遷御史、給事中。

translations.literal: He successively served as vice director and director, was transferred to censor and supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through vice director and director, then moved to the Censorate and the Office of Scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，出為廣東督糧道，調雷瓊道，歷山東、浙江按察使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he went out as grain superintendent of Guangdong, was transferred to the Lei-Qiong circuit, and successively served as provincial judicial commissioner of Shandong and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he became Guangdong grain superintendent, then Lei-Qiong circuit intendant, and later provincial judicial commissioner in Shandong and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，巡撫吳文鎔薦宗漢可重用，遷甘肅布政使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng, Governor Wu Wenrong recommended Zonghan as fit for heavy responsibility; he was transferred to provincial administrative commissioner of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianfeng, Governor Wu Wenrong recommended Zonghan for greater responsibility, and he was made Gansu administrative commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二年，擢雲南巡撫，未之任，調浙江。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted to governor of Yunnan, did not take up the post, and was transferred to Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was promoted to governor of Yunnan but never took up the post and was transferred to Zhejiang instead.

sentences.zh: 值試辦海運，湖郡漕船淺滯，改留變價，虧銀三十餘萬兩，布政使椿壽情急自縊。

translations.literal: It happened that sea transport was being tried; Hu prefecture grain boats ran aground in shallow water, grain was retained and sold for cash, losing more than three hundred thousand taels of silver; Administrative Commissioner Chunshou, in distress, hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: While sea transport was being trialed, grain barges in the Lake districts grounded in shallow water; the cargo was sold locally at a loss of more than three hundred thousand taels, and Administrative Commissioner Chunshou hanged himself in despair.

sentences.zh: 宗漢疏請原米隨新漕運京，允之。

translations.literal: Zonghan memorialized requesting the original grain accompany the new tribute grain to the capital; it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan memorialized that the stranded grain be shipped north with the new tribute fleet; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 三年，粵匪犯江寧，調浙江兵二千名赴援。

translations.literal: In the third year Guangdong bandits attacked Jiangning; he transferred two thousand Zhejiang troops to aid.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, as Taiping forces threatened Jiangning, he sent two thousand Zhejiang troops to reinforce the city.

sentences.zh: 江寧尋陷，宗漢赴嘉興、湖州籌防，疏言不可僅於本境畫疆而守。

translations.literal: Jiangning soon fell; Zonghan went to Jiaxing and Huzhou to organize defense, memorializing that one could not merely guard within one's own borders.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangning soon fell; Zonghan moved to Jiaxing and Huzhou to organize defense and argued that guarding only within provincial borders would not suffice.

sentences.zh: 於是分兵赴江蘇、安徽境內協防，詔嘉其妥協。

translations.literal: Thereupon troops were divided to assist defense within Jiangsu and Anhui; an edict praised his appropriate handling.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent detachments into Jiangsu and Anhui to cooperate in defense, and the court commended his judgment.

sentences.zh: 尋上海匪起陷城，請海運改於劉河受兌。

translations.literal: Soon Shanghai bandits rose and seized the city; he requested that sea transport be changed to receive tribute at Liuhe.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels soon seized Shanghai, he proposed shifting the sea-transport collection point to Liuhe.

sentences.zh: 時江南大營需餉甚鉅，宗漢貽書向榮，通盤籌算，請於江蘇、浙江、江西三省確定每月額數。

translations.literal: At the time the Jiangnan Grand Camp needed funds in huge amounts; Zonghan wrote Xiang Rong, making comprehensive calculations, requesting that Jiangsu, Zhejiang, and Jiangxi fix a monthly quota.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangnan Grand Camp then needed enormous funds; Zonghan wrote Xiang Rong with a comprehensive plan to set fixed monthly quotas from Jiangsu, Zhejiang, and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 榮據以上聞，文宗韙之。

translations.literal: Xiang reported upward; the Wenzong Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang forwarded the plan and the Xianfeng Emperor approved it.

sentences.zh: 四年，特詔褒宗漢辦理防務、海運，及本境治匪、察吏，精詳無瞻顧，深堪嘉尚，特賜御書「忠勤正直」扁額，勉其慎終如始，以成一代良臣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year a special edict praised Zonghan for handling defense, sea transport, and suppressing bandits and inspecting officials within his province with meticulous care and no partiality, deeply worthy of commendation, specially granting an imperial inscription plaque reading "Loyal, Diligent, Upright, and Straightforward," urging him to be careful to the end as at the beginning, to become a fine minister of the age.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year a special edict praised Zonghan's defense work, sea transport, bandit suppression, and official oversight in Zhejiang as meticulous and impartial, deeply admirable, and awarded him an imperial plaque reading "Loyal, Diligent, Upright, and Straightforward," urging him to finish as he had begun and become a statesman of his generation.

sentences.zh: 擢四川總督。

translations.literal: He was promoted to governor-general of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to governor-general of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 給事中張修育疏言：「宗漢治浙，佈置合宜，未可更易。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zhang Xiuyu memorialized, saying: "Zonghan's governance of Zhejiang is well arranged and should not be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zhang Xiuyu memorialized: "Zonghan's administration of Zhejiang is sound and he should not be moved.

sentences.zh: 」詔不允。

translations.literal: " The edict did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: " The court did not agree.

sentences.zh: 會因數月未奏事，降旨詢問，以疾為言，詔斥之，議降三級調用，加恩降二品頂戴，​​仍留總督任。

translations.literal: It happened that because for several months he had not memorialized, an edict was sent to inquire; he pleaded illness; an edict rebuked him, deliberated demotion by three ranks and transfer, but by grace his second-rank cap button was reduced while he still retained the governorship.
translations.idiomatic: When he failed to report for months, the throne demanded an explanation; he pleaded illness and was rebuked, with demotion by three ranks proposed; by imperial grace he kept the governorship with a reduced second-rank cap button.

sentences.zh: 五年，馬邊夷匪為亂，平之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Mabian Yi bandits rebelled; he pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he suppressed a Yi uprising at Mabian.

sentences.zh: 遵旨遣松潘鎮總兵德恩以兵二千援荊州，又調兵四千赴貴州剿苗，並協餉十萬兩。

translations.literal: Following orders he sent Songpan Brigade Commander De'en with two thousand troops to aid Jingzhou, also transferred four thousand troops to Guizhou to suppress Miao, and jointly supplied one hundred thousand taels of funds.
translations.idiomatic: On orders he sent Songpan brigade commander De'en with two thousand men to aid Jingzhou, dispatched four thousand troops to Guizhou against the Miao, and forwarded one hundred thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 六年，復因久無奏報，命將軍樂斌查奏，以痰疾聞，下部議降調，命來京另候簡用。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, again because of long absence of memorials, the General Le Bin was ordered to investigate and report; phlegm illness was reported; the ministry deliberated demotion and transfer; he was ordered to come to the capital to await another appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, after another long silence, General Le Bin was told to investigate; Zonghan cited phlegm illness, the ministry recommended demotion, and he was recalled to Beijing to await a new post.

sentences.zh: 補內閣學士，兼署刑部侍郎、順天府尹。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Secretariat academician, concurrently acting vice minister of Punishments and governor of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a Grand Secretariat academician, concurrently acting vice minister of Punishments and governor of Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 廣東軍事起，葉名琛被擄，授宗漢兩廣總督，兼通商大臣。

translations.literal: Guangdong military affairs arose; Ye Mingchen was captured; Zonghan was appointed governor-general of Liangguang, concurrently superintendent of trade.
translations.idiomatic: When war engulfed Guangdong and Ye Mingchen was taken prisoner, Zonghan was appointed governor-general of the Two Guang and superintendent of trade.

sentences.zh: 時廣州為英人所踞，巡撫柏貴在城中為所脅制。

translations.literal: At the time Guangzhou was occupied by the English; Governor Bai Gui in the city was coerced by them.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou was in British hands; Governor Bai Gui remained inside the city under their control.

sentences.zh: 民團四起，文宗因徐廣縉等前拒英人入城，賴紳民之力，欲復用之，命在籍侍郎羅惇衍、京卿龍元僖、給事中蘇廷魁治團練。

translations.literal: Militia rose everywhere; the Wenzong Emperor, because Xu Guangjin and others had earlier refused English entry into the city and relied on gentry and people's strength, wished to use them again, and ordered retired Vice Minister Luo Dunyan, Court Gentleman Long Yuanxi, and Supervising Secretary Su Tingkui to manage militia training.
translations.idiomatic: Militia sprang up everywhere; recalling how Xu Guangjin had blocked British entry with gentry and commoners, the Xianfeng Emperor ordered retired Vice Minister Luo Dunyan, Court Gentleman Long Yuanxi, and Supervising Secretary Su Tingkui to organize the militia.

sentences.zh: 惇衍等號召鄉團，得數万人，戒期攻城，卒無功；

translations.literal: Dunyan and others summoned village militia, obtained tens of thousands of men, set a date to attack the city, but in the end had no success;
translations.idiomatic: Luo Dunyan and his colleagues raised tens of thousands of village militia and fixed a date to storm the city, but the attempt failed;

sentences.zh: 又禁華人不得受僱為洋人服役以困之。

translations.literal: they also forbade Chinese from being hired to serve foreigners in order to distress them.
translations.idiomatic: they also forbade Chinese to work for foreigners, hoping to strain the occupation.

sentences.zh: 八年春，各國遣人赴江蘇投書致京師大學士訴粵事，請遣大臣至上海會議；

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year the various nations sent men to Jiangsu to deliver letters to grand secretaries in the capital complaining of Guangdong affairs, requesting a high official be sent to Shanghai for negotiations;
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year the foreign powers sent envoys through Jiangsu with letters to Beijing grand secretaries protesting Guangdong affairs and asking that a senior minister come to Shanghai to negotiate;

sentences.zh: 且言逾期即赴天津。

translations.literal: and moreover said that if the deadline passed they would go to Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: they warned that missing the deadline would send them to Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 詔仍回廣東候宗漢查辦，而英、俄兩國兵船已泊吳淞。

translations.literal: An edict still ordered them to return to Guangdong to await Zonghan's investigation and handling, but English and Russian warships had already anchored at Wusong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict still ordered the envoys back to Guangdong for Zonghan to handle, even as British and Russian warships anchored at Wusong.

sentences.zh: 宗漢過江蘇，總督何桂清堅留在上海開議，宗漢不可，遽去；

translations.literal: Zonghan passed through Jiangsu; Governor He Guiqing strongly urged him to remain at Shanghai to open negotiations; Zonghan would not agree and hurried away;
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Jiangsu, Governor He Guiqing pressed him to stay at Shanghai and negotiate; Zonghan refused and hurried on;

sentences.zh: 取道浙、閩，調兵不可得。

translations.literal: taking the route through Zhejiang and Fujian, he could not obtain transferred troops.
translations.idiomatic: traveling through Zhejiang and Fujian, he failed to raise the troops he needed.

sentences.zh: 及至廣東，敵兵已犯天津。

translations.literal: When he reached Guangdong, enemy troops had already attacked Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Guangdong, the allies had already struck Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 宗漢駐惠州，惟恃聯絡民團，出示空言激勵，為英人所禁格，不能遍及。

translations.literal: Zonghan stationed at Huizhou, relying only on linking militia, issuing empty words of encouragement; the English forbade and blocked this, and it could not spread everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan stayed at Huizhou, relying on militia contacts and empty proclamations of encouragement that the British suppressed, so his appeals could not reach the province.

sentences.zh: 既而天津和約成，俟償款六百萬兩分年交畢，始退出廣州，粵民愈憤。

translations.literal: Soon the Tianjin treaty was concluded; only after six million taels indemnity were paid in installments over years did they withdraw from Guangzhou, and Cantonese grew still angrier.
translations.idiomatic: The Tianjin treaty followed; only after six million taels were paid in installments did the allies leave Guangzhou, which left Cantonese still more furious.

sentences.zh: 英領事宣布和議，新安鎮鄉勇殺其張示者數人，遂發兵陷新安。

translations.literal: The English consul announced the peace; Xin'an town militia killed several men who posted the notices, and troops were sent to seize Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: When the British consul posted the peace terms, Xin'an militia killed several men putting up the notices, and British troops seized the town.

sentences.zh: 民團大舉攻城，初勝終挫，懸賞格購洋官首，亦僅時伺隱僻，有所殺傷而已。

translations.literal: Militia launched a great attack on the city; at first victorious, ultimately defeated; rewards were posted for foreign officials' heads, yet they only occasionally lurked in secluded places and caused some casualties.
translations.idiomatic: Militia stormed the city in force, winning early fights but losing in the end; head-money was offered for foreign officers, yet assassins only now and then struck from hiding.

sentences.zh: 宗漢外怵強敵，內畏民嵒，不能有所措施。

translations.literal: Zonghan outwardly feared the strong enemy, inwardly feared the people's wrath, and could take no measures.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan feared the foreigners abroad and the mob at home, and could settle on no policy.

sentences.zh: 泊大學士桂良等至上海議稅則及換約事宜，將與商交還廣州，向宗漢詢近狀，輒不答。

translations.literal: When Grand Secretary Gui Liang and others reached Shanghai to discuss tariffs and treaty revision, intending to negotiate return of Guangzhou, they asked Zonghan about recent conditions, but he repeatedly did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Secretary Gui Liang reached Shanghai to discuss tariffs and treaty revision and to negotiate Guangzhou's return, he asked Zonghan for a report; Zonghan would not reply.

sentences.zh: 而英人以既議和，民團復相仇殺，來相詰問，且揭團紳告示載諭旨有異，必欲去宗漢及三團紳。

translations.literal: But the English, because peace had already been discussed yet militia again killed each other, came to press for explanations, and moreover exposed militia gentry proclamations carrying edicts that differed, insisting on removing Zonghan and the three militia gentry leaders.
translations.idiomatic: The British, citing the peace while militia kept killing one another, demanded explanations and produced gentry proclamations with altered imperial wording, insisting that Zonghan and the three militia leaders be removed.

sentences.zh: 桂良等疏聞，詔責宗漢捕偽造諭旨之人，罷其通商大臣，改授何桂清。

translations.literal: Gui Liang and others memorialized; an edict rebuked Zonghan to arrest those who forged edicts, removed him as superintendent of trade, and replaced him with He Guiqing.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Liang reported upward; an edict ordered Zonghan to arrest the forgers of edicts, stripped him of the trade superintendency, and gave the post to He Guiqing.

sentences.zh: 英使額羅金猶不愜，遽率監赴廣東。

translations.literal: English envoy Elgin was still not satisfied and abruptly led supervisors to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Elgin, still dissatisfied, abruptly led officials back to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 九年，遂復有天津之役。

translations.literal: In the ninth year there was again the Tianjin campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year fighting at Tianjin broke out again.

sentences.zh: 尋調宗漢四川總督，召至京，改以侍郎候補。

translations.literal: Soon Zonghan was transferred to governor-general of Sichuan, summoned to the capital, and changed to vice minister awaiting substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan was soon named Sichuan governor-general, recalled to the capital, and reduced to vice-minister awaiting appointment.

sentences.zh: 十年，署吏部侍郎，尋實授。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he acted as vice minister of Personnel, and soon received substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he served as acting vice minister of Personnel and soon received full appointment.

sentences.zh: 四川京官呈請飭赴四川督辦團練，不許。

translations.literal: Sichuan capital officials submitted a request ordering him to proceed to Sichuan to supervise militia training; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Beijing officials from Sichuan petitioned that he return to organize militia there; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 宗漢與載垣、端華、肅順等交結。

translations.literal: Zonghan associated with Zaiyuan, Duanhua, Sushun, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan cultivated ties with Zaiyuan, Duanhua, Sushun, and their faction.

sentences.zh: 十一年，穆宗即位，載垣等獲罪。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Muzong Emperor ascended the throne; Zaiyuan and others were condemned.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the Tongzhi Emperor succeeded; Zaiyuan and his allies fell.

sentences.zh: 少詹事許彭壽疏劾宗漢與陳孚恩、劉昆並黨肅順等，踪跡最密。

translations.literal: Junior Mentor Xu Shoushou memorialized impeaching Zonghan together with Chen Fu'en and Liu Kun as party to Sushun and others, their tracks most intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Mentor Xu Shoushou impeached Zonghan along with Chen Fu'en and Liu Kun as intimate associates of Sushun's clique.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「黃宗漢本年春赴熱河，危詞力阻回鑾。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Huang Zonghan this spring went to Rehe, using alarming words to strenuously obstruct the return of the imperial procession.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Huang Zonghan went to Rehe this spring and used alarming language to block the return of the imperial procession.

sentences.zh: 迨皇考梓宮將回京，又以京城可慮，遍告於人，希冀阻止。

translations.literal: When His Late Father's coffin was about to return to the capital, he again said the capital was to be feared, telling everyone widely, hoping to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: When the late emperor's coffin was about to reach Beijing, he again warned that the capital was unsafe and spread the story everywhere, hoping to delay the move.

sentences.zh: 其意存迎合載垣等，眾所共知。

translations.literal: His intention was to curry favor with Zaiyuan and others, as all knew.
translations.idiomatic: His aim was plainly to curry favor with Zaiyuan's faction, as everyone understood.

sentences.zh: 聲名品行如此，若任其濫廁卿貳，何以表率屬僚？

translations.literal: With reputation and conduct such as this, if he were allowed to clutter the ranks of ministers, how could he set an example for subordinates?
translations.idiomatic: With reputation and conduct such as this, how could he be allowed to remain among senior ministers and set an example for the bureaucracy?

sentences.zh: 革職永不敘用，以為大僚輭媚者戒。

translations.literal: Strip office and never again employ, to serve as a warning to grand officials who fawn and flatter.
translations.idiomatic: Strip his office permanently as a warning to grandees who fawn on power.

sentences.zh: 」並追奪前賜御書「忠勤正直」扁額。

translations.literal: " And moreover posthumously revoked the earlier granted imperial plaque "Loyal, Diligent, Upright, and Straightforward."
translations.idiomatic: " The court also revoked the earlier imperial plaque "Loyal, Diligent, Upright, and Straightforward."

sentences.zh: 同治三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongzhi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Tongzhi.

sentences.zh: 論曰：當道、咸之間，海禁大開，然昧於外情，朝野一也。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Between Daoguang and Xianfeng, the maritime prohibition was greatly opened, yet ignorant of foreign conditions—court and country alike.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Between the Daoguang and Xianfeng reigns the maritime frontier opened wide, yet court and country alike remained blind to foreign realities.

sentences.zh: 粵民身創夷患之深，目擊國威之墮，憤懼交乘，遂因拒入城一事，釀成大釁。

translations.literal: Cantonese people personally suffered the depth of barbarian calamity, witnessed the fall of national prestige, anger and fear multiplying together, and thus because of the matter of refusing entry into the city brewed a great quarrel.
translations.idiomatic: Cantonese had felt the foreign assault at first hand and watched national prestige collapse; rage and fear fed each other until the refusal to admit foreigners into the city ignited a full-scale crisis.

sentences.zh: 朝廷誤信民氣可用，而不知虛聲之不足恃也。

translations.literal: The court mistakenly believed popular spirit could be used, yet did not know empty reputation was not to be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: The court mistook popular fervor for usable strength and did not see that bluster alone could not be trusted.

sentences.zh: 徐廣縉操縱有術，幸安一時；

translations.literal: Xu Guangjin manipulated with skill and was fortunate to secure peace for a time;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guangjin handled the foreigners with skill and secured a temporary peace;

sentences.zh: 葉名琛狃於前事，驕愎致敗，宜哉。

translations.literal: Ye Mingchen clung to past affairs, pride and obstinacy brought defeat—as was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Mingchen clung to his earlier triumph until pride and obstinacy brought ruin—as he deserved.

sentences.zh: 黃宗漢依違貽誤，終以依附權要被譴。

translations.literal: Huang Zonghan wavered and caused delay, in the end punished for attaching to the powerful faction.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zonghan wavered until delay became disaster and was punished at last for clinging to the ruling clique.

sentences.zh: 廣縉在粵東剿平羅鏡匪有功，及代賽尚阿督師，軍事已壞，旁皇失措，咎無可辭焉。

translations.literal: Guangjin in eastern Guangdong suppressed and pacified the Luojing bandits with merit; when he replaced Sai Shang'a to command troops, military affairs were already ruined, flustered and at a loss—blame cannot be excused.
translations.idiomatic: Guangjin earned credit suppressing the Luojing rebels in eastern Guangdong, but when he replaced Sai Shang'a in command the war was already lost; his panic and indecision admit no excuse.
